video_title: Golfing with LeBron & Kevin Hart & Summer League Standouts With Draymond Green

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green clarifies his golf score with LeBron James and Kevin Hart
quotes.excerpt: I didn't shoot a 123. When I walked up, Kevin said, 'Draymond, what you shoot a 123?'
quotes.quote: There is this common misconception going around the internet that I shot a 123. Where you all are wrong is, I didn't shoot a 123. When I walked up, Kevin said, 'Draymond, what you shoot a 123?' And I said, '123?' He said, 'Yeah, you shot a 123.' I said, 'No, I didn't shoot a 123.' I said, 'What you shoot?' He said, '119.' He was trying to beat LeBron and Steve Stoute to the punch of saying what he shot. So he threw it out there. I'm like, 'Whoa, I didn't expect that he shot a 119.' So I'm like, 'Oh, shit. You shot a 119?' He said, 'Yeah, I shot a 119, and what you shoot? What's your score?' Once he announced his 119, I was baffled because the last time I shot a 119, it was a while ago.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green evaluates Yaxel's potential fit on the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: When you have length and some athleticism and you can shoot the ball, there's always a spot.
quotes.quote: Yaxel has been balling, averaging 17 and 7 boards. The Dubs are having a good Summer League. I've seen all the talk like, 'Where does he fit on the Warriors this upcoming year?' And the reality is, when you have length and some athleticism and you can shoot the ball, there's always a spot. You will find minutes wherever you need to. There's always a spot for that. Where does he fit? I don't know. That'll get figured out as you put the pieces in the place and who plays together. There's so much more that goes into that, but with that skill set, there's always a spot. There's always a role.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green critiques Yaxel's pitch to LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: I know you don't like rookies that much, but I'm not the average rookie.
quotes.quote: A lot of people I saw like, 'Oh man, Yaxel gave his pitch to LeBron.' He said, 'I know you don't like rookies that much, but I'm not the average rookie. If you're looking to play with the greatest shooter of all time and Draymond, we'll be glad to have you.' Is the pitch too weak or too strong? I don't know. I think the pitch is pointless. Training camp is coming soon enough and you got to rein the rook in a little bit. You know, teach him a few things.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green explains why Caleb Wilson's floor is Kevin Garnett
quotes.excerpt: When I said, 'Yo, Caleb Wilson's floor could be Kevin Garnett,' everybody like, 'Yo, you're an idiot.'
quotes.quote: When I said, 'Yo, Caleb Wilson's floor could be Kevin Garnett,' everybody like, 'Yo, you're an idiot.' And I'm like, 'No, let me help you understand why I said Caleb Wilson's floor could be Kevin Garnett.' Because Caleb Wilson comes in an era where big men can dribble the ball, big men can shoot threes. Big men pretty much have free rein if you can do it to do whatever you want. Kevin Garnett didn't have that. Kevin Garnett played in a very structured era of basketball where the power forward shot 18 to 20 footers and they banged down low just like a center, and Kevin Garnett banged with those guys. And Kevin Garnett is one of the greatest power forwards we've ever seen, top three power forward we've ever seen. And so when I said Caleb Wilson, Kevin Garnett could be the floor, I said that with all due respect to Kevin Garnett. But just saying, yo, this kid can be that special.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green analyzes the new-look Trail Blazers backcourt
quotes.excerpt: It's a great backcourt. I think ultimately you have to figure out how does that work.
quotes.quote: We haven't truly discussed Ja Morant to the Blazers. Their backcourt now consists of Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson, and Shaedon Sharpe, which I think is a great backcourt. I think ultimately you have to figure out how does that work, right? Like, who's guarding bigger? Obviously we know Scoot can guard bigger, but between Damian Lillard, Shaedon Sharpe, and Scoot, who's going to guard bigger? How do you make those lineups work, you know, together? As opposed to like, 'Oh man, when Shaedon's on, Damian Lillard's not.' How do you, what can you do to make those lineups work together? Who are the other pieces around them to make those lineups work together? Because I think ultimately that's going to be the key to figuring out how well this fit works, how good ultimately this team can be.
